A1.justification: Both PDFs describe CARP and contain readable main text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices. Retained content can be matched across relocation and renumbering, supporting a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original simulation benchmarks, trajectory analyses, inference measurements, and real-world UR5e manipulation results.

after.justification: v3 retains those empirical results and adds Push-T, FurnitureBench, Franka robot experiments, ablations, and additional analyses.

M1.justification: The per-dimension multi-scale VQ-VAE, residual quantization, GPT-style next-scale predictor, and training losses remain unchanged. Collective decoding of all scales clarifies the residual aggregation already present in v1's Algorithm 1; the PDFs do not establish a redesigned method.

E1.justification: v3 adds Push-T for contact-rich, multimodal pushing and FurnitureBench assembly tasks One Leg, Round Table, and Lamp, including physical One Leg execution on a Franka Panda. These substantially broaden task requirements and real-world embodiment coverage while retaining the original benchmarks.

E2.justification: Appendix F newly evaluates VQ-BeT and Consistency Policy against CARP on Kitchen and Push-T; their citations in v1 were not evaluated comparisons. Figure 12 also introduces LSTM-GMM into the data-efficiency comparison. These additions materially strengthen comparison with efficient alternatives.

E3.justification: New protocols include 30–200-demonstration subsampling, K=1–6 scale experiments with feature-map expansion, 1,024 FurnitureBench rollouts per task, and single-task Nut-Assembly/Threading evaluation using first-contact position errors. Push-T visualization uses top-3 sampling. These extend evaluation design; the original benchmarks retain their principal horizons and training budgets.

E4.justification: Beyond v1's trajectory/refinement visualization, v3 adds scale sensitivity, joint versus per-dimension tokenizer reconstruction analysis, data-efficiency tests, training and inference cost breakdowns, recovery and hesitation failure cases, and insertion-precision analysis. These directly investigate design choices, efficiency, and failure conditions.

E5.justification: Tables 8–9 newly report means and variances of first-contact position errors, adding descriptive dispersion statistics. The original top-three-checkpoint averaging and five timing runs remain; neither version provides systematic multi-seed confidence intervals or significance testing.

E6.justification: v3 adds substantial result sets for the new benchmarks, baselines, ablations, and precision studies. For example, Figure 5 reports Push-T success rates of 0.88 for CARP, 0.87 for DP-C, and 0.84 for DP-T. Most original benchmark values remain, but Table 3 changes DP-T's Kitchen p2 score from 0.99 to 0.98.

T1.justification: The mathematical substance of Equations 1–9 and the residual quantization algorithm is retained. Prediction notation and explanatory corrections do not introduce new assumptions, derivations, theorems, or proofs.

C1.justification: The central contribution and abstract's performance and speed claims remain. The introduction newly claims comparable multimodal behavior, while RQ2 drops fast convergence and focuses specifically on inference efficiency.

C2.justification: Appendix D distinguishes inference advantages from training convergence and tokenizer pretraining costs. Appendix G explains recovery failures through missing failure demonstrations and hesitation through short observation histories. Appendix A shifts from underdeveloped multimodal potential to claimed comparable expressiveness, while questioning how strongly existing benchmarks require multimodality.

D1.justification: Most training recipes in Appendix H are relocated from v1. New disclosures include the three-dimensional task embedding, argmax versus top-3 sampling, exclusion of visual encoders from parameter counts, and training hardware and resource accounting. Appendix K also documents AprilTag-based state estimation for the added real-world experiments.

R1.justification: v3 adds FurnitureBench and From Imitation to Refinement references for the assembly experiments and explicitly discusses comparison with VQ-BeT and Consistency Policy, both already cited in v1. The broader positioning around VAR-inspired autoregression and diffusion policies remains stable.

P1.justification: The main section sequence and most method exposition remain intact. v3 tightens prose, clarifies decoding and efficiency terminology, condenses related work, and consolidates existing experimental implementation paragraphs in Appendix H. Much of the appendix expansion consists of new scientific content rather than rewriting retained material.

P2.justification: v3 adds numerous analytical plots, comparison tables, failure illustrations, and assembly visualizations. It also merges the original single-task and multi-task setup figures into Figure 4, combines real-world setup and results in Figure 7, and relocates the original UR5 execution visualization to Appendix K.

improvement.justification: v1 largely supported CARP through benchmark scores and trajectory examples. v3 substantially strengthens validation through efficient competing baselines, design ablations, cost accounting, multimodal pushing, another physical robot, and explicit failure analysis. These additions make the central performance–efficiency claims more assessable and better qualified. Limited uncertainty reporting and unexplained differences between Nut-Assembly scores in Tables 4 and 8 remain, but do not outweigh the substantial evidential gains.
